2. Opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed the aforesaid Miscellaneous case for preemption of 1.64 acres of land mentioned in Schedule Nos. 1, 2, and 3 of the pre-emption petition under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Their case is that they are co-sharers of the properties of Schedule Nos. 1 and 2 as heirs of their father and contiguous owners of Schedule No.3 property as heirs of their father who was owner of plot Nos. 94, 95, 96, 104, 101 and 102. Petitioner purchased the said 1.64 acres of land from the vendor opposite party No. 3 by registered sale deed dated 4.8.83 at a consideration of Taka 2000.00. After coming to know about the sale opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed the case on depositing the consideration money with statutory compensation 

 Pre-emptor-opposite parties deposited the price of the land stated in the sale deed dated 4.8.83 executed and registered in pursuance of the decree for specific performance of contract for sale of the case land made on 27.2.65 and not the price of the land prevailing at the time of execution and registration of the disputed sale deed on 4.8.83. Undoubtedly, it is a great hardship to the petitioner to be deprived of the case land without being paid the price of the land prevailing at the time of execution and registration of the disputed sale deed. But section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act having not provided relief for such circumstances it is not within the power of this Court to mitigate such hardship. It is for the Legislature to amend the law to give relief in such circumstances causing hardship to such purchaser of land.
